scope: Read-only native flat64 aggregate sizing over emitted binary descriptors. No whole instruction admission, allocation/work/virtual-heap policy, private-source proof or exception-state integration.
adaptations: binary_size.c adapts all thirteen kind branches in the sizing phase of interpreter i_bs_create_bin. Native append kinds exclude their prefix; fixed/string sizes, binary-all type/length, flat64 dynamic size and UTF8/16/32 ordering remain intact. The ARCH_32 alternative is not admitted on the existing flat64-only target. No partial dispatch case is enabled by this component.

Borrowed explicit X/Y spans replace register macros. Descriptor count/kinds/units/flags/fixed widths and register bounds are checked before semantic sizing. Y includes the continuation slot, which cannot be read as an operand. These checks are not current-frame/must-definition, pointer-provenance or private-source-consumption proof. Inputs must remain stable and serialized.

Typed returned failures replace BS_FAIL_INFO exception jumps, carrying kind, segment, reason, info and borrowed offending value. The existing error-payload factory roots that value when called; the sizing result does not retain it or set process exception state. Invalid metadata and infrastructure ceiling refusal are distinct from native badarg/system_limit.

Native BS_SAFE_MUL retains both compiler-builtin and unsigned multiply/quotient paths. Negative/noninteger sizes are badarg; positive big sizes, product overflow and a product outside signed-word range are system_limit. Cumulative addition is checked against an explicit caller ceiling instead of wrapping. A reached ceiling is reported only after all native sizing checks, preserving later sizing errors before allocation refusal.

UTF8 and UTF16 deliberately use native tagged-word estimates without scalar validation. The construction writer must still reject invalid scalars. UTF32 performs the native early scalar check. Sizing does not eagerly check binary-all unit divisibility, fixed-field source types or float widths that native construction validates later.

Tests cover all kinds, exhaustive scalar range including surrogate/out-of-range behavior, 10000 independent unsigned128 multiplication checks, aggregate word overflow, late-error precedence, register limits and maximum descriptor count. Real emitted string/literal descriptors feed the sizer and writers. C-owned mixed construction reloads X/Y after GC and executes identity BEAM; a borrowed big error value survives payload collection and OOM retry with exact retirement.

A separate eleven-case stock exception oracle records ten matching cases on installed OTP28/ERTS16.3 ARM JIT. Invalid UTF8 followed by negative integer size differs: stock reports segment1/utf8/type, while the pinned interpreter sizing phase defers UTF8 validation and reports segment2/integer/size. The pinned ARM JIT source also performs early UTF8 validation. The runner records the mismatch explicitly; it does not normalize outputs or claim all-reference conformance. No newly built pinned interpreter or cross-version/backend execution witness is claimed.
